issues.quote: He worked on it for four years.
issues.fact: The fact sheet gives no duration for the repeater's construction.
issues.misreading: A solver could take the four-year figure as a timeline clue, for example about when the work began or how long the master had been preoccupied with it. It is not tied to any clock reading.

issues.quote: He meant it to strike the first minute of the new century.
issues.fact: The fact sheet says nothing about what the repeater was meant to strike or when.
issues.misreading: The line adds a specific timing intention for the watch that the sheet does not provide, which a solver could treat as a hint about the repeater's intended strike time.

issues.quote: He was not a man who would be late for anything.
issues.fact: The fact sheet says only that the master sent her downstairs when the regulator showed twenty past ten and that he was well. It says nothing about his punctuality.
issues.misreading: The remark is a characterization that could push a solver to read the master's timing as strictly punctual, which would shape how the clock readings are interpreted.

issues.quote: Mine was exact. I regulated it myself.
issues.fact: The fact sheet says only that her watch was exact at nine.
issues.misreading: The added claim that she regulated the watch herself suggests a personal reliability guarantee that the sheet does not give.
